title: Credit-based sink throttling for OTLP/gRPC exporters to contain tail-latency amplification
creator: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: We observe occasional tail-latency amplification in the OTLP/gRPC path when downstream tracing sinks (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party vendors) briefly degrade. Current retries and local buffering exacerbate bursts and increase end-to-end latency for critical requests. This ticket implements a credit-based, per-sink throttling protocol and local scheduler so ingress can respect downstream capacity and avoid amplification while preserving best-effort delivery for lower-priority trace payloads.
background: Existing OTLP exporters use size/time-based batching with local queueing and exponential backoff. When a sink's gRPC path slows (e.g., GC events, transient network congestion, vendor throttles), simultaneous retries from many exporter workers create short overload spikes. We've seen this correlate with increases in 99th/99.9th p50/p90 parse & write latencies in the serving runtime and SLO alerts during cross-region incidents.
design_summary: Introduce a lightweight credit exchange layer between collector instances and sink-facing exporter clients. Credits represent allowed bytes/requests per-sink per-window. Exporter workers consume credits before sending; collectors periodically refresh credits based on sink health signals (gRPC status, observed RTT, explicit sink heartbeats). When credits are low, exporters throttle, shift low-priority traces to best-effort async paths, and emit detailed metrics for circuit state. The protocol is backward-compatible: when the collector doesn't advertise credits, exporters fall back to current behavior.
implementation_steps: Define credit message schema and extension in OTLP collector-to-exporter control channel
Add credit-aware queue to exporter clients with policy hooks for priority tagging (route, tenant, sample rate, critical vs non-critical)
Integrate sink health heuristics: gRPC p50/p90 latency, gRPC error rate, application-level 429/503 responses, socket-level backpressure signals
Expose control plane API to set static credit caps per-sink (for enterprise dedicated/private customers)
Instrument telemetry: credit_grants, credit_consumed, drain_rate, queued_payload_bytes, throttled_spans_by_priority
Unit tests and integration harness that simulates sink slowdown and validates no tail amplification and eventual-delivery guarantees
Create dashboard and alerting rules for credit exhaustion and high throttle durations
Canary rollout with 10% of exporters -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if p99 latency worsens
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: added control messages increase complexity and slight control-plane load. Mitigation: control messages are small and rate-limited; default fallbacks preserve behavior.
Tradeoff: strict crediting enforces availability at the cost of possibly delaying non-critical spans. We rely on priority tagging to preserve user-facing traces.
Operational risk: misconfigured static caps for dedicated customers could underutilize capacity. Mitigation: provide dry-run telemetry and per-sink suggested caps computed from historical throughput.
Compatibility risk with 3rd-party sinks that expect existing semantics. Mitigation: feature gated; collectors will only advertise credits to upgraded exporters; provide CLI toggle for integrators.
acceptance_criteria: Exporters correctly consume and respect credits in unit and integration tests
Simulated sink slowdown test: serving runtime p99/p999 latency improves >=30% vs baseline without crediting
End-to-end trace delivery: high-priority traces preserved; low-priority traces eventually delivered or dropped with audit logs
Metrics emitted (credit_grants, credit_consumed, throttled_spans) and dashboard panels created
Canary rollout plan executed and rollback playbook documented
Compatibility fallback test: collectors not advertising credits do not break exporters
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for credit accounting and queue transitions. 2) Integration harness: OSS tempo local sink + simulated pathological sink that delays gRPC responses. 3) Chaos test: randomly drop control messages and assert graceful fallback. 4) Load test: 50k spans/s with busybox sized spans to validate metrics and behavior under peak. 5) Regression sweep for memory/queue growth.
dashboard_and_alerts: New panels under Observability > Traces > Exporter Flow Control: credit_grants/time, credit_headroom_by_sink, throttled_spans_by_tenant, exporter_queue_depth. Alerts: ExporterCreditExhausted (>=5m), ExporterThrottlingHigh (throttled_spans_rate > 0.5% for 10m).
rollout_plan: Feature gate default-off. Canary group 1 (dev clusters) -> telemetry review -> canary group 2 (prod test tenants) -> phased enable for low-risk tenants -> full rollout. Use circuit breaker to instantly disable crediting if p99 increases. Rollback steps documented in runbook.
docs_and_announce: Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Credit+Based+Exporter+Flow+Control . Slack thread: #observability-runtime thread ID 8792. Customer announcement draft for dedicated/private customers with instructions to set static caps.

notes: This approach intentionally keeps changes minimal in the public OTLP wire path; credits are exchanged via a small control channel between our collector/control-plane and exporter runtime. For private deployments we also offer a static cap override so security teams can enforce egress limits. Work aligns with broader initiative observability-exporter-resilience.
